part: P5A Part 15 -- Scalable Identity Digest Reconciliation
objective: Prove, via streaming/chunked digests (not loading 5.2M rows into memory at once), that UNION(HOT rows in replacement_main.db, COLD rows across all 41 segments) contains EXACTLY the same set of transfer_index rows as production transfer_index at frozen high-water id <= 6648855.
method: Streamed each source (production, replacement_main.db, each of the 41 cold segment files) in ascending-id chunks of 100,000 rows via sqlite3 fetchmany(). For each row computed SHA256 over the identity tuple, then combined all row digests within and across chunks/sources using XOR (commutative + associative, so chunk boundaries and HOT/COLD/segment partitioning cannot affect the final combined digest). Peak memory footprint per source pass = one 100k-row chunk, never the full 5.2M-row set.

identity_key_investigation.v1_result: FALSE-POSITIVE MISMATCH -- row counts matched exactly (5,223,038 = 5,223,038) but digest did not match
identity_key_investigation.root_cause_found: cold_segments/*.sqlite intentionally use a FRESH local `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` per segment file (confirmed by direct inspection: transfer_index_cold_2026_04.sqlite ids run 1..727605, unrelated to the original production id). This is correct behavior per src/ops/transfer_cold_store.py's COLD_SCHEMA, which declares the true row identity as `UNIQUE (signature, source, destination)`, not `id`.
identity_key_investigation.additional_finding: signature alone is not unique per row either -- confirmed a single cold segment (2026_04) has 727,605 rows but only 147,641 distinct signatures (multiple transfer legs can share one tx signature), so signature alone is an insufficient key.
identity_key_investigation.v2_corrected_key: (signature, source, destination, amount_lamports, block_time) -- composite tuple matching each row's full copied identity, used consistently across production, HOT, and every COLD segment

cold_segments.note: per-segment row counts recorded in raw_result_file; largest segments are the most recent months (2026_04 = 727,605 rows, 2026_03 = 245,207, 2026_02 = 204,038), smallest are the earliest historical months (single-digit rows in 2009-2023 range) -- consistent with organic production growth over time

note: Digest and row count match EXACTLY between production transfer_index (id<=6648855) and the P5A HOT+COLD union using the corrected composite identity key. No missing or unexplained rows found. This satisfies the Part 15 hard-stop gate: identity reconciliation did NOT find missing/unexplained rows, so no hard-stop was triggered.
